arxiv-2106-00478.title: Space-average electromagnetic fields and EM anomaly weighted by energy density in heavy-ion collisions
arxiv-2106-00478.creator: Irfan Siddique, Xin-Li Sheng, Qun Wang
arxiv-2106-00478.description: Abstract We study the space-average electromagnetic (EM) fields weighted by the energy density in the central regions of heavy ion collisions. These average quantities can serve as a barometer for the magnetic-field induced effects such as the magnetic effect, the chiral separation effect and the chiral magnetic wave.

arxiv-2110-03485.title: Cartoon Explanations of Image Classifiers
arxiv-2110-03485.creator: Stefan Kolek, Duc Anh Nguyen, Ron Levie, Joan Bruna, Gitta Kutyniok
arxiv-2110-03485.description: Abstract We present CartoonX (Cartoon Explanation), a novel model-agnostic explanation method tailored towards image classifiers and based on the rate-distortion explanation (RDE) framework. Natural images are roughly piece-wise smooth signals—also called cartoon-like images—and tend to be sparse in the wavelet domain.

arxiv-2111-03488.title: SLA-Driven Load Scheduling in Multi-Tier Cloud Computing: Financial Impact Considerations
arxiv-2111-03488.creator: Husam Suleiman and Otman Basir
arxiv-2111-03488.description: Abstract A cloud service provider strives to effectively provide a high Quality of Service (QoS) to client jobs. Such jobs vary in computational and Service-Level-Agreement (SLA) obligations, as well as differ with respect to tolerating delays and SLA violations. The job scheduling plays a critical role in servicing cloud demands by allocating appropriate resources to execute client jobs.

arxiv-2209-14422.title: StacerBot: A Stacktrace Search Engine for Stack Overflow
arxiv-2209-14422.creator: Md Abdullah Al Alamin
arxiv-2209-14422.description: Abstract We as software developers or researchers very often get stacktrace error messages while we are trying to write some code or install some packages. Many times these error messages are very obscure and verbose; do not make much sense to us.

arxiv-2403-05451.creator: Amir M. Mansourian, Arya Jalali, Rozhan Ahmadi, Shohreh Kasaei
arxiv-2403-05451.description: Abstract Deep learning models have achieved significant results across various computer vision tasks. However, due to the large number of parameters in these models, deploying them in real-time scenarios is a critical challenge, specifically in dense prediction tasks such as semantic segmentation.

arxiv-2408-08114.title: Quantifying the informativity of emission lines to infer physical conditions in giant molecular clouds
arxiv-2408-08114.creator: Lucas Einig, Pierre Palud, Antoine Roueff, Jérôme Pety, Emeric Bron, Franck Le Petit, Maryvonne Gerin, Jocelyn Chanussot, Pierre Chainais, Pierre-Antoine Thouvenin, David Languignon, Ivana Bešlić, Simon Coudé, Helena Mazurek, Jan H. Orkisz, Miriam G. Santa-Maria, Léontine Ségal, Antoine Zakardjian,
arxiv-2408-08114.description: Abstract Context. Observations of ionic, atomic, or molecular lines are performed to improve our understanding of the interstellar medium (ISM). However, the potential of a line to constrain the physical conditions of the ISM is difficult to assess quantitatively, because of the complexity of the ISM physics.

arxiv-2411-03449.title: AI Horizon Scanning – White Paper p3395 Part III. Technology Watch: a selection of key developments, emerging technologies, and industry trends in Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-2411-03449.creator: George Tambouratzis, Marina Cortês, Andrew R. Liddle
arxiv-2411-03449.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by George Tambouratzis, Marina Cortês, Andrew R. Liddle. Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies are in a phase of unprecedented rapid development following the landmark release of Chat-GPT, which brought the phenomenon to wide public attention.

arxiv-2506-15375.title: Learning to Maximize Quantum Neural Network Expressivity via Effective Rank
arxiv-2506-15375.creator: Juan Yao
arxiv-2506-15375.description: Abstract Quantum neural networks (QNNs) are widely employed as Ansätze for solving variational problems, where their expressivity directly impacts performance. Yet, accurately characterizing QNN expressivity remains an open challenge, impeding the optimal design of quantum circuits. In this work, we introduce the effective rank, denoted as κ \kappa , as a novel quantitative measure of expressivity.

arxiv-2507-18885.title: IsaMini: Redesigned Isabelle Proof Lanugage for Machine Learning
arxiv-2507-18885.creator: Qiyuan Xu 1 , Renxi Wang 2 , Haonan Li 2 , David Sanán 3 , and Conrad Watt 1
arxiv-2507-18885.description: Abstract Neural Theorem Proving (NTP) employs deep learning methods, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), to automate formal proofs in proof assistants. This approach holds promise for reducing the dramatic labor costs or computation costs required in proof engineering, which is fundamental to formal verification and other software engineering methods.

arxiv-2601-21633.title: A Tilted Seesaw: Revisiting Autoencoder Trade-off for Controllable Diffusion
arxiv-2601-21633.creator: Pu Cao, Yiyang Ma, Feng Zhou, Xuedan Yin, Qing Song, Lu Yang
arxiv-2601-21633.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Pu Cao, Yiyang Ma, Feng Zhou, Xuedan Yin, Qing Song, Lu Yang. In latent diffusion models, the autoencoder (AE) is typically expected to balance two capabilities: faithful reconstruction and a generation-friendly latent space (e.g., low gFID). In recent ImageNet-scale AE studies, we observe a systematic bias toward generative metrics in handling this trade-off: reconstruction metrics are increasingly under-reported, and ablation-based AE selection often favors the best-gFID configuration even when reconstruction fidelity degrades.

Irgm1 (LRG-47) is an interferon-inducible Golgi membrane associated GTPase of the mouse whose disruption causes susceptibility to many different intracellular pathogens. Irgm1 has been variously interpreted as a regulator of homologous effector GTPases of the IRG family, a regula

plos-pone-0012452.title: CREB Inhibits AP-2α Expression to Regulate the Malignant Phenotype of Melanoma
plos-pone-0012452.creator: Vladislava O. Melnikova, Andrey S. Dobroff, Maya Zigler et al.
plos-pone-0012452.description: PLOS ONE research article. The loss of AP-2α and increased activity of cAMP-responsive element binding (CREB) protein are two hallmarks of malignant progression of cutaneous melanoma. However, the molecular mechanism responsible for the loss of AP-2α during melanoma progression remains unknown. Herein, we

pmc-10503066.title: Divergent functions of NLRP3 inflammasomes in cancer: a review
pmc-10503066.creator: Alireza Shadab, Mohamad Mahjoor, Mohammad Abbasi-Kolli, Hamed Afkhami, Parisa Moeinian, Amir-Reza Safdarian
pmc-10503066.description: The cancer is a serious health problem, which is The cancer death rate (cancer mortality) is 158.3 per 100,000 men and women per year (based on 2013–2017 deaths). Both clinical and translational studies have demonstrated that chronic inflammation is associated with Cancer progression. However, the precise mechanisms of inflammasome, and the pathways that mediate this phenomenon are not fully characterized.

pmc-10656241.title: Promoting couples’ resilience to relationship obsessive compulsive disorder (ROCD) symptoms using a CBT-based mobile application: A randomized controlled trial
pmc-10656241.creator: Milana Gorelik, Ohad Szepsenwol, Guy Doron
pmc-10656241.description: Relationship Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (ROCD) is a disabling form of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) centering on interpersonal relationships. Previous findings suggest ROCD symptoms are particularly detrimental to romantic relationships. In this randomized controlled trial (RCT), we assessed influence a CBT-based mobile application used by both partners on resilience to ROCD symptoms, cognitions, and relationship dissatisfaction.

pmc-11300873.title: Human response to the Younger Dryas along the southern North Sea basin, Northwest Europe
pmc-11300873.creator: Philippe Crombé, Camille Pironneau, Prudence Robert, Pierre van der Sloot, Mathieu Boudin, Isabelle De Groote, Sophie Verheyden, Hans Vandendriessche
pmc-11300873.description: Currently in NW Europe little is known about the human response to the extensive cold reversal at the end of the Pleistocene, the Younger Dryas (ca. 12,850 till ca. 11,650 cal BP), mainly due to the poor chronological resolution of the archaeological sites belonging to the Ahrensburgian Culture.

pmc-11470516.title: Cabozantinib prevents the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis by inhibiting the activation of hepatic stellate cell and macrophage and attenuating angiogenic activity
pmc-11470516.creator: Takuya Matsuda, Kosuke Kaji, Norihisa Nishimura, Shohei Asada, Aritoshi Koizumi, Misako Tanaka, Nobuyuki Yorioka, Yuki Tsuji, Koh Kitagawa, Shinya Sato, Tadashi Namisaki, Takemi Akahane, Hitoshi Yoshiji
pmc-11470516.description: Cabozantinib, a multiple tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting AXL, vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR), and MET, is used clinically to treat certain cancers, including hepatocellular carcinoma. This study aimed to assess the impact of cabozantinib on liver fibrosis and hepatocarcinogenesis in a rat model of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH).

pmc-12733744.title: The Effects of Subalpine Forest Succession on Soil Fungal Community Composition and Diversity Vary with Soil Depth and Trophic Mode on the Eastern Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau
pmc-12733744.creator: Miao Chen, Jian Chen, Xiaoqiang Tang, Shun Liu, Hongshuang Xing, Xuhua Li, Lei Cai, Zhengjingru Xu, Wenhao Miao, Xia Hu, Qiuhong Feng, Xin Zhang
pmc-12733744.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Soil fungi play an indispensable role in maintaining soil ecosystem functions. However, how forest succession and soil depth interactively shape fungal community composition and diversity remains poorly understood. To address this, we investigated fungal communities across four successional stages and two soil depths (0–10 cm and 40–60 cm) in a subalpine forest on the eastern Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau using Illumina high-throughput sequencing. Results showed that the soil fungal community composition of different trophic modes varied significantly with both succession and soil depth.

pmc-13289497.title: Explainable prediction of MDR/RR-TB in tuberculosis-diabetes mellitus multimorbidity: a machine learning model developed and validated in a dual-center study
pmc-13289497.creator: Xinxin Zhong, Kuan Liu, Jiujin Zhang, Xinhua Tang, Tao Lu, Qiqi Chen, Jianzhi Pang, Rongjun Chen, Bingrou Li, Siyuan Ding, Libing Ma
pmc-13289497.description: BackgroundTuberculosis-diabetes mellitus (TB-DM) multimorbidity significantly increases the risk of multidrug-resistant/rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB). Early risk stratification tools for this high-risk population remain lacking.ObjectiveTo develop and validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) model for predicting MDR/RR-TB in patients with TB-DM multimorbidity, and to identify key predictive factors using explainable artificial intelligence.

pmc-13599084.title: Small bowel necrosis caused by migrated intrauterine device: a rare surgical emergency
pmc-13599084.creator: Juan Zhang, Ying-mei Xiao, Mao-Juan Wang, Fan Jiang, Min Chen, Xia-hong Huang
pmc-13599084.description: BackgroundThe intrauterine device (IUD) is an efficient and commonly used long-term contraceptive method. Although generally safe, its rare yet serious complications—uterine perforation and secondary intra-abdominal migration—can lead to injuries to adjacent organs, such as intestinal perforation, obstruction, or necrosis. IUD displacement into the small intestine causing necrosis is an extremely rare clinical event, with limited reports in the literature.

pmc-13606751.title: Circulating Tumor Function: A Systems Biology Framework for Liquid Biopsy in Genitourinary Cancers
pmc-13606751.creator: Roxana Andra Coman, Andreea Nutu, Lia-Raluca Olari, Stefan Strilciuc, Dana Monica Iancu, Ioana Berindan-Neagoe
pmc-13606751.description: Liquid biopsy enables minimally invasive detection and longitudinal monitoring of tumor-derived material in blood and urine. In genitourinary cancers, most applications have focused on genomic alterations in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), together with circulating tumor cells (CTCs), extracellular vesicles (EVs), and cell-free RNAs.
